messages:
maya: heads up — canary 3.2.1 seeing steady RSS growth on streaming-chat after ~2h, KV resident_pages keep increasing despite eviction ops appearing normal
aj: repro steps?
maya: send a long tool-loop input (multi-turn tool calls, average seq ~9k). I ran it on g4-canary-01, pid 4421
maya: top snapshot:
```
KV: resident_pages=1,234,567 evict_ops=98,412 reclaim_rate=95% pages_free=2.4%
heap: rss=15.2G pss=14.7G
```
ryan: interesting — reclaim 95% but pages_free low. maybe fragmentation or page anchoring? did you check page chain lengths?
maya: yes, page chain lengths spike during heavy tool-loops, and perf shows pagewalk latency bursts: `pagewalk: 2.7ms` every ~10s
sam: could be allocator failing to coalesce after frequent small frees. any recent kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes?
maya: we rolled `fastpath_batch_v2` two days ago on canary, which changed batching alignment. suspect it affects chunk packing in KV pages
aj: can you attach a perf flame or pprof? even a short `perf record -g` of the spike would help
maya: uploaded perf sample to /tmp/pprof-kv-4805.pb and pushed snapshot to s3; small snippet of the hotpath: 
```
# hot paths from pprof
kv_page_walk
kv_realloc
memcpy
kv_page_pin
```
ryan: try forcing defrag pathway: set `KV_DEFRAG=1` and rerun tool-loop. also run `kvctl inspect --dump-fragmentation` every 5m
maya: starting defrag run now
infra-bot: snapshot saved to s3://redwood-canary-snapshots/4805001234/ (tag: auto)
maya: preliminary: RSS stabilizes for ~30m then creeps again. defrag reduced chain_count by ~18% but not full fix. pagewalk bursts still present
sam: can you capture slab histograms and page occupancy distribution? small-object churn could leave many tiny holes
maya: slab histo attached:
```
slab_64: 12M alloc 11.9M used
slab_256: 1.2M alloc 1.1M used
slab_1k: 4k alloc 3.9k used
page_usage: 78% avg, tail buckets at 38%
```
aj: hypothesis: batching alignment change made allocations prefer offsets that split objects across page boundaries leading to half-used pages under long contexts. That increases fragmentation even with high reclaim counts
ryan: action items: (1) reproduce on node with old batching config, (2) run with `KV_DEFRAG=1` and `KV_DEFRAG=2` to toggle aggressiveness, (3) collect `pmap` + perf flame during the 2h window, (4) try `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512` override to reduce batch size and test effect on fragmentation
maya: will run A/B today across two canaries and post results here
sam: adding to backlog INF-7623 and tagging runtime/allocator and eng-runtime on the ticket
maya: quick question — any risk flipping `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS` on canary while traffic is live? :thinking_face:
aj: low risk, but watch tail latency. if throughput drops we should rollback. this is our fastest knob to test alignment effect
maya: kicking off A/B now, will post perf + slab dumps in ~3h
